claude.country: Multi-country (US AREDS images; clinicians from 12 institutions; external validation in Singapore)
claude.sample_unit: patients (AREDS patient samples; 960 images, 2880 AMD risk features, 24 clinicians)

links.outcome: Clinician diagnostic accuracy (F1) and time with vs without AI assistance for AMD features
links.effect: AI assistance improved accuracy for 23 of 24 clinicians; mean F1 rose from 37.71 to 45.52; time saved 10.3 s per patient; combining manual and AI did not always yield highest accuracy or efficiency.
links.quote: AI assistance significantly improved accuracy for 23 of 24 clinicians, increasing the mean F1 score from 37.71 (95% CI, 27.83-44.17) to 45.52 (95% CI, 39.01-51.61), with some improvements exceeding 50%.

links.outcome: AI model performance on external Singapore cohort versus other test sets
links.effect: Original model underperformed on the external Singapore cohort; DeepSeeNet+ had a significantly higher F1 score than the original model there (52.43 vs 38.95).
links.quote: The DeepSeeNet+ model performed better in 3 test sets, achieving a significantly higher F1 score than the Singapore cohort (52.43 [95% CI, 44.38-61.00] vs 38.95 [95% CI, 30.50-47.45]).

links.outcome: F1 score of model after retraining with additional US images, tested on 3 datasets including external
links.effect: DeepSeeNet+ trained on 39,196 additional images performed better in 3 test sets, with F1 52.43 vs 38.95 in the Singapore cohort.
links.quote: The DeepSeeNet+ model performed better in 3 test sets, achieving a significantly higher F1 score than the Singapore cohort (52.43 [95% CI, 44.38-61.00] vs 38.95 [95% CI, 30.50-47.45]).
